subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures remain accepted asynchronously and then terminalize with a typed startup failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup before returning accepted?
rationale: Both designs can fix the visible hang, but the choice changes the `sessions_spawn` acceptance contract, registry lifecycle state, gateway wait behavior, and the overlapping startup-silence work.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep the accepted async spawn contract, but emit and persist a typed startup failure visible through subagent/session tools and gateway waits.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Validate enough Docker sandbox startup before returning accepted, trading lower ambiguity for more latency and compatibility risk in the spawn call.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox-specific proof case while the broader startup lifecycle design is settled elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted async spawn contract, but emit and persist a typed startup failure visible through subagent/session tools and gateway waits.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history in subagent spawn, registry, gateway, and lifecycle code touched by this contract choice.
